lede: Brand guidelines, or the brand style guide, are the rulebook that keeps a brand consistent everywhere: logo, colour, type, voice and how they all behave. We write guidelines your whole team can actually follow, so the brand stays sharp long after we hand it over.

faq.a: Brand guidelines, also called a brand style guide, are the rules that keep a brand consistent: how to use the logo, colour, type, voice, imagery and motion, with clear do's and don'ts. They let anyone represent the brand correctly without having to ask.

faq.q: What is the difference between brand guidelines and a brand style guide?
faq.a: They are two names for the same thing. 'Brand style guide' tends to emphasise the visual rules; 'brand guidelines' often adds voice and behaviour too. We build the full version either way.

At minimum: logo usage, colour, typography, and do's and don'ts. A complete set also covers voice and tone, imagery, graphics and motion, with real examples of the brand applied. Yours are scoped to what your team actually needs.

The moment more than one person makes anything with your brand, the answer is yes. A designer, a freelancer, a printer, a new hire: guidelines are what stop a brand drifting into inconsistency and losing recognition.

faq.q: How much do brand guidelines cost?
faq.a: Guidelines come with every identity we design, and our brand work starts at $280. A standalone guide for an existing brand is quoted to scope. See the full pricing.

closing.note: Tell us about the brand and who needs to use it. We will write the guidelines that keep it unmistakable.
